invariants: Flow.id matches ^[a-z0-9-]+/[a-z0-9-]+$ (product slug '/' flow slug), so every id is two lowercase path segments and no two flows share one

Flow.canonical_url == '/flows/' + Flow.id for every Flow; the '/' inside the id stays a literal path separator and is never percent-encoded, so /flows/leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline is the link for leafcutter/flow-render-pipeline
Exactly one Flow has is_default_entry == true, and it is leafcutter/deliver-a-feature (the flow the bare /flows view opens on today)
Every Flow.drills_into[].flow resolves to a Flow.id, and Flow.drills_into[].step names the step of that Flow whose drill affordance opens it

FlowRoute.resolution == 'default-entry' iff FlowRoute.requested_flow_id == null; such a route renders the is_default_entry Flow, keeps address_bar == '/flows', answers http_status 200 and starts from today's filters {source: real, kind: user, realization: all}

FlowRoute.resolution == 'selected' iff FlowRoute.requested_flow_id resolves to a Flow.id; then rendered_flow == requested_flow_id, address_bar == that Flow.canonical_url followed by '?step=' + requested_step when requested_step != null, http_status == 200 (a legacy link answers 308 instead, see redirect_to), and filters == {source: Flow.source, kind: Flow.kind, realization: all} so the flow selector lists the linked flow instead of falling back to the first flow of today's filters

FlowRoute.resolution == 'not-found' iff FlowRoute.requested_flow_id != null and resolves to no Flow.id; then rendered_flow == null and crumbs == [] (the view never silently renders the default entry or any other flow), http_status == 404, address_bar == requested_url (the bad link stays visible so it can be corrected), and notice != null
FlowRoute.notice != null iff FlowRoute.resolution == 'not-found'; notice.detail quotes requested_flow_id verbatim and notice.action_href == '/flows'

FlowRoute.crumbs == [rendered_flow] whenever rendered_flow != null: a canonical URL names one flow, not the drill path it was reached by, so a freshly opened link shows that flow as the entry with no parent trail
FlowRoute.entered_via == 'ac-detail-link' iff FlowRoute.link_source != null; link_source resolves to a FlowAppearance.id and requested_url == that FlowAppearance.href

FlowRoute.requested_step == the ?step= value of requested_url, verbatim (for a legacy link, its &step= value); null when requested_url names no step. requested_flow_id never includes the query: it is the path after '/flows/' (for a legacy link, the percent-decoded ?flow= value)

A ?step= value (FlowRoute.requested_step, FlowAppearance.node_id) is looked up among the steps AND branches of its flow: within one flow, step ids and branch ids never collide (the explorer keys both as step:<id>), and a branch opens the same drawer a step does

FlowRoute.open_drawer != null iff rendered_flow != null and requested_step names a step or branch of rendered_flow; then open_drawer == requested_step: the page opens on that flow with that node's drawer open (one drawer at most)

FlowRoute.step_notice != null iff rendered_flow != null, requested_step != null and requested_step names no step or branch of rendered_flow; then open_drawer == null, the flow still renders as a selected route (http_status 200, crumbs == [rendered_flow], notice == null, the unknown ?step= stays in address_bar), step_notice.title == 'Step not found' and step_notice.detail quotes requested_step verbatim
FlowRoute.resolution == 'not-found' implies open_drawer == null and step_notice == null: a ?step= on an unknown flow id is not looked at, only the 'Flow not found' notice shows

FlowRoute.redirect_to != null iff requested_url is a legacy '/flows?flow=<id>&step=<step>' link (the form the AC drawer emitted before, the id's '/' percent-encoded as %2F); then redirect_to == '/flows/' + requested_flow_id + '?step=' + requested_step with the id's '/' literal, http_status == 308 (permanent redirect, so the legacy URL never stays in the tab's history), address_bar == redirect_to, and resolution, rendered_flow, crumbs, filters, open_drawer, notice and step_notice equal those of the FlowRoute whose requested_url == redirect_to (present in this dataset). redirect_to == null for every other route

FlowAppearance.href == the Flow.canonical_url of FlowAppearance.flow_id + '?step=' + FlowAppearance.node_id, for steps and branches alike, so following it opens that flow with that node's drawer open; it never uses the legacy /flows?flow=...&step=... form, and two appearances share an href only when they name the same node of the same flow
FlowAppearance.flow_name == the Flow.name of FlowAppearance.flow_id
FlowAppearance.node_id names a step (node_kind == 'step') or a branch (node_kind == 'branch') of flow_id whose implements[] contains FlowAppearance.ac, and node_label is that node's label
FlowAppearance.id == FlowAppearance.ac + '@' + FlowAppearance.flow_id + '#' + FlowAppearance.node_id

Within one FlowNavigation.session, seq starts at 1 and increases by 1; seq 1 is the only record with action == 'load' and history_op == 'initial', and its history_stack holds exactly one URL at history_index 0
FlowNavigation.address_bar == FlowNavigation.history_stack[FlowNavigation.history_index] for every record

FlowNavigation.history_op == 'push' iff action in {select, drill, crumb}: history_stack == the previous record's history_stack cut after its history_index, plus the new address_bar, and history_index == previous history_index + 1 (pushing drops any forward entries). A push lands on the target Flow.canonical_url with no ?step= and drawer == null, also when a drawer was open (selecting or drilling from an open drawer closes it), and the entry it leaves keeps the URL last replaced into it

FlowNavigation.history_op == 'replace' iff action in {open-drawer, close-drawer}: history_stack == the previous record's history_stack with only the entry at history_index rewritten to the new address_bar (forward entries are kept, none is added), and history_index, rendered_flow, crumbs and shows are unchanged, so opening, switching or closing a drawer never adds a Back-button entry

FlowNavigation.history_op == 'pop' iff action in {back, forward}: history_stack is unchanged, history_index moves by -1 (back) or +1 (forward), and address_bar, rendered_flow, crumbs, shows and drawer equal those of the latest earlier record that wrote that history position (the load, a push or a replace): Back and Forward move between flow-level entries, and an entry's drawer is whatever was last replaced into it

FlowNavigation.shows == 'graph' iff rendered_flow != null; then rendered_flow == the last of crumbs and address_bar == that Flow.canonical_url, followed by '?step=' + drawer when drawer != null, except the bare '/flows' entry which renders the default-entry Flow with no drawer; shows == 'not-found' iff rendered_flow == null, crumbs == [] and drawer == null

FlowNavigation.drawer == the ?step= value of address_bar when that value names a step or branch of rendered_flow, and drawer == null when address_bar carries no ?step=: at most one drawer is open and the address bar always shares exactly what is on screen (a link whose ?step= names no step of the flow keeps that ?step= in address_bar with drawer == null, as route-unknown-step shows)

FlowNavigation.action == 'open-drawer' implies drawer names a step or branch of rendered_flow, drawer != the previous record's drawer and address_bar == Flow.canonical_url of rendered_flow + '?step=' + drawer: opening a different step's drawer while one is open swaps the one ?step= value instead of adding a second
FlowNavigation.action == 'close-drawer' implies the previous record's drawer != null, drawer == null and address_bar == Flow.canonical_url of rendered_flow with no query

FlowNavigation.action == 'drill' implies via_step != null, the previous record's rendered_flow has a drills_into entry {step: via_step, flow: rendered_flow}, and crumbs == previous crumbs + [rendered_flow]; via_step == null for every other action
FlowNavigation.action == 'select' implies crumbs == [rendered_flow]; action == 'crumb' implies crumbs is the previous crumbs cut after rendered_flow

fields.kind: enum: user | data | architecture — drives the Kind filter
fields.source: enum: real | mock — drives the Source filter
fields.realization: enum: built | spec | mock — drives the Realization filter and the realization banner
fields.level: enum: journey | pipeline | agent — the level chip (journey → pipeline → agent = drill deeper)
fields.canonical_url: string — '/flows/' + id; the one shareable address of this flow
fields.is_default_entry: boolean — true only for the flow the bare /flows view opens on
fields.drills_into: array of { step, flow } — each step whose drill affordance opens a sub-flow, and that sub-flow's Flow.id (first expands_to target)

fields.entered_via: enum: nav-link | address-bar | shared-link | ac-detail-link — nav-link == the sidebar 'Flows' link; address-bar == typed or bookmarked; shared-link == opened from outside the Atlas (chat, ticket, PR); ac-detail-link == an 'Appears in flows' link in the AC detail drawer

fields.redirect_to: string | null — for a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link, the step link it redirects to (/flows/<id>?step=<step>); null for every other URL
fields.rendered_flow: string | null — Flow.id drawn on the canvas; null only for not-found
fields.crumbs: array of Flow.id — the breadcrumb trail right after the page opens; [] for not-found
fields.open_drawer: string | null — the step or branch id whose drawer is open right after the page opens; null when the URL names no step, names one the flow does not have, or the flow is not found
fields.address_bar: string — the URL the address bar shows once the view has resolved (redirect_to after a legacy redirect)
fields.http_status: integer — what requested_url answers: 200 when a flow renders (also when its ?step= names no node), 404 for an unknown flow id, 308 for a legacy ?flow= link (permanent redirect to redirect_to)
fields.filters: object { source, kind, realization } — the Source / Kind / Realization filter state right after the page opens
fields.notice: object | null — the not-found state { title, detail, action_label, action_href }; null unless resolution == not-found
fields.step_notice: object | null — the 'Step not found' notice { title, detail } shown over a rendered flow whose ?step= names no step or branch of it; null otherwise

provenance.note: Created: no canonical dataset existed for Flow in ux-prototyping (by_entity.Flow.canonical_mock_data was empty; ux-prototyping's only dataset, fern-and-fig/catalog, models Plant/Customer/Order/Payment). THE canonical dataset for the Atlas /flows view and its canonical flow URLs (/flows/<flow id>). Flow records mirror twelve real flows in docs/product-truth/flows/ (names, kind, source, realization, level and expands_to drill targets as stored; leafcutter/deliver-a-feature is the DEFAULT_ENTRY in leafcutter-web/components/flows/flows-view.tsx). FlowRoute covers every way the view can be opened: the bare /flows default entry; shared, bookmarked and AC-drawer links to real/mock, journey/pipeline/agent and architecture flows (filters follow the linked flow); step links (/flows/<flow id>?step=<node id>) that open the flow with a step's or a branch's drawer open; a step id the flow does not have (the flow opens with no drawer and a 'Step not found' notice); four unknown flow ids (a typo, a product name alone, a step appended as a path segment, a typo carrying ?step=) that show a 404 not-found state instead of falling back; and a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link (as the AC drawer emitted it, id percent-encoded) that redirects with 308 to the step link. FlowAppearance mirrors real AC-drawer 'Appears in flows' entries (one flow, two flows, three steps of one flow, and two branch appearances), each pointing at <canonical url>?step=<node id> instead of today's /flows?flow=...&step=... query that FlowsView ignores. FlowNavigation walks three browser sessions: drill-and-return (push, back, forward, breadcrumb push dropping the forward entry), a shared mock journey (drill, select, back twice) and recovering from an unknown id (back returns to the not-found state). Revised 2026-10-08 before the first commit, per the owner's mock-data-gate decision (approved with one edit to assumption 5): a step link is /flows/<flow id>?step=<stepId> and opens that flow with that step's drawer open; the AC drawer's 'Appears in flows' links use that form; old /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> links redirect to the new URL; a step id the flow does not have opens the flow without a drawer and says the step was not found. Branches use the same ?step= form because the explorer opens the same drawer for a branch as for a step (flow-step-view.ts keys both as step:<id>; no flow has a step and a branch with the same id). Assumptions 1-4 unchanged: bare /flows keeps its URL and shows the default flow; an unknown flow id answers 404 with a 'Flow not found' notice quoting the id, a link back to /flows and the selector, drawing no other flow; opening a flow link sets the Source and Kind filters to that flow's, Realization all; a fresh link shows only that flow in the breadcrumb and back/forward restore each entry's breadcrumb. Not modelled: assumption 6 (a filter change that makes a different flow render); a legacy ?flow= link without &step=. Extend this dataset; do not start a second Flow dataset.

Extended to v2 per the owner's decision at the mockup gate on 2026-10-09, verbatim: "Opening a step's drawer writes ?step=<id> into the address bar and closing it removes it, using history 'replace' (no new back-button entries) — the current URL always shares exactly what you see. Selecting or drilling to another flow still pushes a new entry." The owner also confirmed two details v1 already models: a legacy /flows?flow=<id>&step=<step> link answers a permanent 308 redirect (route-legacy-step-link), and an unknown ?step= stays visible in the address bar (route-unknown-step). FlowNavigation gains a drawer field (the step or branch whose drawer is open, null when none; every v1 record has drawer null), two actions, open-drawer (a click on a step or branch, also to swap one open drawer for another) and close-drawer (the drawer's X button or a click beside it), and the history_op replace, which rewrites the current entry in place, keeps forward entries and adds none. Select, drill and crumb still push, always to the target flow's canonical URL with no ?step=. Three sessions show it: drawer-replace (open a flow, open the 'Plan' drawer, switch to 'Build', close it, drill into the build pipeline; one Back press returns to the flow with no drawer, because the three drawer actions added no entries); drawer-in-history (a step link from an AC drawer opens with the drawer, the drawer's 'Open sub-flow' button pushes the sub-flow with no ?step=, Back reopens the drawer because that entry still carries ?step=code, closing it replaces the entry, and after Forward then Back the flow returns with no drawer); select-from-open-drawer (picking another flow in the selector while a drawer is open pushes that flow's URL with no ?step=, and Back restores the drawer). New invariants cover replace, open-drawer, close-drawer and drawer == ?step=; the push, pop and graph invariants now include the drawer. Still not modelled: assumption 6 (a filter change that makes a different flow render); a legacy ?flow= link without &step=; opening a drawer on the bare /flows entry (the rules as written replace it with /flows/leafcutter/deliver-a-feature?step=<id>, which the owner has not ruled on); whether the 'Step not found' notice of an unknown ?step= link clears when a real step's drawer is opened. Today's drawer lays a scrim over the canvas that closes it on click, so switching straight from one drawer to another (nav-drawer-replace-3) needs the click to reach the other step.
